Like most of your videos, they are interesting. You make many valid points, but I don't generally fully agree with your conclusions. AI in 2026 in my opinion is not intelligence. AI programs are tremendously complex, nearly infinite electrical power consuming , and very expensive syntax guessing machines. This machine can accomplish some very impressive parlor tricks but it is not a thinking machine. Yes, AI may replace or augment some software coders, some artists and animators , some actors in video commercials, movies and TV, but jobs that require serious thought and especially discernment and judgement, not so much.

I think it's a tech that has potential to be useful but needs safeguards, just like social media has its pros, but needs safeguards. Or at least to not be allowed to actively make their product addictive.
